title: The First Aorist
subtitle: ἔλυσα — the basic past tense for completed action.
objectives: Conjugate any regular ω-verb in the first aorist indicative active and middle.
Understand the aorist as the simple past tense for completed action.
Recognize the augment ἐ- and the sigma infix as the markers of the first aorist.
Distinguish aorist from imperfect by meaning: completed versus ongoing past action.

sections.heading: The aorist tense
sections.body:
The aorist is the simple past tense. ἔλυσα means 'I loosed' or 'I freed'. The aorist expresses completed action in past time, without regard to duration. The imperfect expresses ongoing or repeated past action; the aorist expresses a single, completed past action.

English 'I was loosing' = Greek imperfect ἔλυον.
English 'I loosed' = Greek aorist ἔλυσα.

The aorist is formed with the augment ἐ-, the sigma infix (like the future), and a new set of endings called the secondary active endings.

sections.heading: The first aorist indicative active: ἔλυσα
sections.body:
singular
  1st   ἔλυσα       I loosed
  2nd   ἔλυσας      you loosed
  3rd   ἔλυσε(ν)    he/she/it loosed

  plural
  1st   ἐλύσαμεν    we loosed
  2nd   ἐλύσατε     you (plural) loosed
  3rd   ἔλυσαν      they loosed

The endings are -α, -ας, -ε(ν), -αμεν, -ατε, -αν. These are the first aorist endings.

sections.heading: The first aorist indicative middle: ἐλυσάμην
sections.body:
singular
  1st   ἐλυσάμην    I freed myself
  2nd   ἐλύσω       you freed yourself
  3rd   ἐλύσατο     he/she/it freed himself/herself/itself

  plural
  1st   ἐλυσάμεθα   we freed ourselves
  2nd   ἐλύσασθε    you (plural) freed yourselves
  3rd   ἐλύσαντο    they freed themselves

The endings are -άμην, -ω, -ατο, -άμεθα, -ασθε, -αντο.

sections.heading: From Xenophon
sections.body:
Anabasis I.1.2: ἐγένετο πόλεμος.
'War arose.' ἐγένετο is the aorist middle of γίγνομαι (I become). The aorist marks a single completed event: 'it came into being', 'it happened'.

What is the difference between the aorist and the imperfect?
items.answer: Aorist: completed action. Imperfect: ongoing or repeated action.

sections.heading: Up next
sections.body: Lesson 3.6 introduces the second aorist. The second aorist is the strong aorist with thematic endings, learned as a separate stem. ἔλαβον (I took), ἦλθον (I came), εἶδον (I saw) are all second aorists. They do not have the sigma infix.

lesson_completion.criteria: Mark the lesson complete when you can conjugate the first aorist active and middle of any ω-verb from memory and can distinguish aorist from imperfect by meaning.
